followUp.question: You inherit a vector index with no notes. Which two of these practices would you check first, and how?
rubric: model and version per vector|which model made the vectors|provenance
approximate recall against exact search|compare with exact search|ANN recall
recall on a labelled set|test queries|measure retrieval

transfer.scenario: Search results suddenly got worse after a vendor quietly updated its embedding model behind the same API name. What do you check and change?
rubric: query and stored vectors from different versions|version mismatch|vectors not comparable
check model version per vector|stored provenance
pin the model version|use a versioned model id
re-run recall on the test set|measure retrieval

narration.text: Documents and queries are embedded with the same model, using its document and query input types.
The vectors come back normalized to length one, so cosine similarity and dot product rank results the same way.
Our index uses approximate search, which can miss a few true nearest neighbors in exchange for speed.
We measured that by comparing its top ten with an exact search on a sample of queries.
Dropping from 1,024 to 512 dimensions halved the size of the stored vectors, and we kept it because recall on our test set barely moved.
Our next model isn't documented as sharing a vector space with this one, so we'll re-embed the whole corpus into a new index.
Every stored vector records the name and version of the model that produced it.
A similarity cutoff tuned for one model always gets retuned for the next, because score scales differ.
